physics/ch-01.title: The four rules of field lines
physics/ch-01.trick: **"Plus se shuru, minus pe khatam, kabhi na kaatein, kabhi na ghoomein"**
meaning: Lines **start on +** and **end on −**.
They **never cross** (one direction of E at a point) and **never form closed loops** (electrostatic field is conservative).
physics/ch-01.prompt: State four properties of electric field lines.

physics/ch-01.title: Axial or equatorial: which is bigger?
physics/ch-01.trick: **"A for Axial, A for Aage (ahead), A for twice"**: axial field = 2 × equatorial field
meaning: Short dipole: $E_\text{axial}=\dfrac{2kp}{r^3}$ along $\vec p$; $E_\text{equatorial}=\dfrac{kp}{r^3}$ opposite to $\vec p$.
physics/ch-01.prompt: At the same distance, how does the axial field of a short dipole compare with the equatorial field?

physics/ch-01.title: Which charges count for flux?
physics/ch-01.trick: **"Flux mein sirf andar wala ginta hai"** (for flux, only the charge inside counts)
meaning: Total flux $=q_\text{enclosed}/\varepsilon_0$; charges outside add zero net flux.
But the **field** on the surface still depends on every charge, inside and outside.
physics/ch-01.prompt: Does a charge outside a closed surface change the total flux through it?

physics/ch-01.title: Which charges count for flux?
meaning: "Flux mein sirf andar wala ginta hai": only the charge inside a closed surface sets the total flux.

physics/ch-02.title: Series and parallel for capacitors
meaning: Capacitors in **series** add as reciprocals ($\frac1C=\frac1{C_1}+\frac1{C_2}$); in **parallel** they simply add.
Resistors do exactly the reverse.
physics/ch-02.prompt: How do capacitors combine in series and in parallel?

physics/ch-02.title: Battery connected or removed?
physics/ch-02.trick: **"Jude raho to V wahi, tod do to Q wahi"** (stay connected: V same; cut off: Q same)
meaning: Connected: $V$ fixed, so $C$, $Q$, $U$ all × K.
Disconnected: $Q$ fixed, so $C$ × K while $V$, $E$, $U$ ÷ K.
physics/ch-02.prompt: When a dielectric is inserted with the battery disconnected, which quantity stays fixed?

physics/ch-02.title: Dielectric inserted: battery on or off?
physics/ch-02.trick: Dielectric inserted: battery on or off?
meaning: "Jude raho to V wahi, tod do to Q wahi": connected keeps V fixed (C, Q, U × K); removed keeps Q fixed (V, E, U ÷ K).

physics/ch-03.title: Ohm's law
meaning: $V=IR$, with $R=\rho\dfrac lA$ and $\rho=\dfrac{m}{ne^2\tau}$.
physics/ch-03.prompt: Write Ohm's law and the expression for resistivity from the drift model.

physics/ch-03.title: What each Kirchhoff rule conserves
meaning: **Junction rule** = conservation of **charge**: no charge piles up at a point.
**Loop rule** = conservation of **energy**: back at the start, back to the same potential.
physics/ch-03.prompt: Which conservation law does each of Kirchhoff's rules express?

physics/ch-03.title: What do Kirchhoff’s rules conserve?
meaning: "Junction pe charge, loop pe energy": junction rule = charge conservation; loop rule = energy conservation.

physics/ch-04.title: Direction of the force on a current
physics/ch-04.trick: **Fleming's left hand = "FBI"**: Thumb = **F**orce, First finger = **B** (field), middle finger = **I** (current)
meaning: Hold the three at right angles; the thumb gives the force on a current-carrying wire (or a positive charge's motion along I).
For an electron, the force is the other way.
physics/ch-04.prompt: Which rule gives the force on a current in a magnetic field, and what does each finger show?

physics/ch-04.title: Do parallel currents attract or repel?
physics/ch-04.trick: **"Ek hi disha, pakke dost"** (same direction, close friends)
meaning: Currents in the **same** direction **attract**; opposite currents repel.
It is the reverse of charges, where like charges repel.
physics/ch-04.prompt: Do two parallel wires carrying current in the same direction attract or repel?

physics/ch-04.title: Where does the extra resistance go?
physics/ch-04.trick: **"Ammeter ko chhota shunt, Voltmeter ko bada resistor"**
meaning: Ammeter: a **small** resistance in **parallel** (shunt).
Voltmeter: a **large** resistance in **series**.
physics/ch-04.prompt: How is a galvanometer converted into an ammeter and into a voltmeter?

physics/ch-05.title: How dia, para and ferro behave in a field
physics/ch-05.trick: **"Dia dur bhaage, Para paas aaye, Ferro fida ho jaaye"**
meaning: **Dia**: runs away (repelled, $\chi<0$).
**Para**: comes a little closer (weakly attracted, small $\chi>0$).
**Ferro**: falls for it completely (strongly attracted, $\chi\gg1$).
physics/ch-05.prompt: How do dia-, para- and ferromagnetic materials behave in a non-uniform magnetic field?

physics/ch-05.title: The four ferromagnets
physics/ch-05.trick: **"Fe-Co-Ni ki Gaadi"** → Fe, Co, Ni, Gd
meaning: Iron, cobalt, nickel and gadolinium are ferromagnetic.

physics/ch-05.title: Dia, para, ferro in one line
physics/ch-05.trick: Dia, para, ferro in one line
meaning: "Dia dur bhaage, Para paas aaye, Ferro fida ho jaaye": repelled, weakly attracted, strongly attracted.

physics/ch-06.title: What does Lenz's law say?
physics/ch-06.trick: **"Lenz = ladne wala"**: the induced current always fights the change
meaning: N pole comes in → near face becomes **N** (repels). N pole goes away → near face becomes **S** (attracts back).
It opposes the **change**, not the field; that is energy conservation.
physics/ch-06.prompt: State Lenz's law and the face polarity when a north pole approaches a coil.

physics/ch-06.title: Fleming's right hand or left hand?
physics/ch-06.trick: **"Right hand for geneRator, Left hand for motor (Left = Lagao force)"**
meaning: Right-hand rule gives the direction of the **induced current** in a moving conductor.
Left-hand rule (FBI) gives the **force** on a current.
physics/ch-06.prompt: Which of Fleming's rules gives the direction of an induced current?

physics/ch-06.title: Lenz’s law in one line
meaning: "Lenz = ladne wala": the induced current always fights the change in flux. N comes in → near face N; N goes away → near face S.

physics/ch-07.title: Who leads in L and in C?
meaning: In an inductor (**L**), voltage **E** comes before current **I**: current lags by $\pi/2$.
In a capacitor (**C**), current **I** comes before voltage **E**: current leads by $\pi/2$.
physics/ch-07.prompt: In a pure inductor, does the current lead or lag the voltage, and by how much?

physics/ch-07.title: Condition for resonance
meaning: Resonance: $X_L=X_C$, so $Z=R$ (minimum) and $I=V/R$ (maximum), $\cos\phi=1$.
$\omega_0=1/\sqrt{LC}$; needs both L and C.
physics/ch-07.prompt: What is the condition for resonance in a series LCR circuit, and what happens to the current?

physics/ch-07.title: Who leads in L and in C?
physics/ch-07.trick: Who leads in L and in C?
meaning: "ELI the ICE man": in L, E (voltage) before I; in C, I before E. The lead or lag is always π/2.

physics/ch-08.title: How are E and B related in an EM wave?
physics/ch-08.trick: **"E aur B saath saath, par ek doosre se tedhe"** (together in time, crossed in direction)
meaning: $E$ and $B$ are **in phase** and **perpendicular** to each other and to the direction of travel.
physics/ch-08.prompt: State the phase and direction relation between E and B in an EM wave.

physics/ch-08.title: Order of the EM spectrum
physics/ch-08.trick: **"Raging Martians Invaded Venus Using X-ray Guns"**
meaning: Radio, Microwave, Infrared, Visible, Ultraviolet, X-rays, Gamma: increasing frequency, decreasing wavelength.
physics/ch-08.prompt: Arrange the EM spectrum in order of increasing frequency.

physics/ch-08.title: Order of the EM spectrum
meaning: "Raging Martians Invaded Venus Using X-ray Guns": radio → gamma, increasing frequency.

physics/ch-09.title: Cartesian sign convention
physics/ch-09.trick: **"Roshni ki disha mein plus"** (along the light, plus)
meaning: Measure from the pole; along the incident light is **+**, against it is **−**; above the axis **+**.
So $u$ is always negative; concave mirror and concave lens have negative $f$.
physics/ch-09.prompt: State the Cartesian sign convention for mirrors and lenses.

physics/ch-09.title: Focal lengths in microscope and telescope
meaning: Microscope: both focal lengths short ($f_o<f_e$).
Telescope: objective long ($f_o$ big), eyepiece short.
physics/ch-09.prompt: Compare the focal lengths of the objective and eyepiece in a microscope and in a telescope.

physics/ch-09.title: Focal lengths: microscope vs telescope
meaning: "Microscope: chhota-chhota; Telescope: bada-chhota": microscope f_o < f_e (both short); telescope f_o ≫ f_e.

physics/ch-10.title: Fringe width in YDSE
physics/ch-10.trick: **"β = λD/d: λ aur D upar, chhota d neeche"** (λ and D on top, small d below)
meaning: Longer wavelength or farther screen → wider fringes; slits farther apart → narrower fringes.
In a medium of index $n$: $\beta'=\beta/n$.
physics/ch-10.prompt: Write the fringe width in YDSE and say how it changes with $\lambda$, $D$ and $d$.

physics/ch-10.title: Interference or diffraction?
physics/ch-10.trick: **"Inter = do (two) sources ke beech; Di-ffraction = ek (one) slit ka mudna"**
meaning: Interference: waves from **two** coherent sources.
Diffraction: wavelets from **one** wavefront bending round an edge.
physics/ch-10.prompt: What is the basic difference between interference and diffraction?

physics/ch-10.title: Interference or diffraction?
meaning: "Inter = two sources ke beech; Di-ffraction = one slit ka mudna": interference needs two coherent sources; diffraction is one wavefront bending.

physics/ch-11.title: Intensity or frequency: what changes what?
physics/ch-11.trick: **"Intensity = Itne electrons (how many); Frequency = Force (how fast)"**
meaning: Brighter light → more photons → larger photocurrent; $V_0$ unchanged.
Higher frequency → more energetic photons → larger $K_\text{max}$ and $V_0$.
physics/ch-11.prompt: How do intensity and frequency each affect the photoelectric current and the stopping potential?

physics/ch-11.title: de Broglie wavelength
meaning: $\lambda=\dfrac hp=\dfrac{h}{mv}=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$; through a voltage $V$: $\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}}$.
physics/ch-11.prompt: Write the de Broglie relation and its form for a charge accelerated through V.

physics/ch-11.title: Intensity or frequency?
meaning: "Intensity = itne electrons; Frequency = force": intensity changes the photocurrent, frequency changes K_max and V₀.

physics/ch-12.title: Kinetic, potential and total energy in an orbit
physics/ch-12.trick: **"K seedha, U do guna ulta"** (K straight, U twice and reversed)
physics/ch-12.prompt: How are the kinetic and potential energies related to the total energy in a Bohr orbit?

physics/ch-12.title: Lower level of each hydrogen series
physics/ch-12.trick: **"Lucknow, Bareilly, Patna, Bhopal, Pune"** → Lyman 1, Balmer 2, Paschen 3, Brackett 4, Pfund 5
meaning: The order of the cities gives $n_f$ = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
Only Lyman is UV and only Balmer is visible; the rest are infrared.
physics/ch-12.prompt: Name the hydrogen series in order of their lower level $n_f$.

physics/ch-12.title: Hydrogen series by lower level
meaning: "Lucknow, Bareilly, Patna, Bhopal, Pune": Lyman 1, Balmer 2, Paschen 3, Brackett 4, Pfund 5.

physics/ch-13.title: Mass–energy conversion
meaning: Multiply a mass defect in u by 931.5 to get the binding energy in MeV.
physics/ch-13.prompt: How much energy, in MeV, is equivalent to 1 u?

physics/ch-13.title: Properties of the nuclear force
meaning: Strongest of all forces; acts only over a few fm; same for n–n, p–p, n–p; each nucleon binds only its neighbours.
Repulsive below about 0.8 fm.
physics/ch-13.prompt: State four properties of the nuclear force.

physics/ch-13.title: Nuclear force in four words
meaning: "S-S-C-S": strongest, short-range, charge-independent, saturating; repulsive below 0.8 fm.

physics/ch-14.title: Which dopant makes which type?
physics/ch-14.trick: **"Paanch se N, Teen se P"** (five gives N, three gives P)
meaning: **Pentavalent** (5 valence electrons: P, As, Sb) → extra electron → **n-type**.
**Trivalent** (3: B, Al, Ga, In) → missing electron (hole) → **p-type**.
physics/ch-14.prompt: Which impurity makes an n-type semiconductor and which makes a p-type one?

physics/ch-14.title: Depletion layer in forward and reverse bias
physics/ch-14.trick: **"Forward mein patla, reverse mein mota"** (thin in forward, thick in reverse)
meaning: Forward bias: barrier and depletion layer get **thinner**, current flows easily.
Reverse bias: both get **wider**, only a tiny current.
physics/ch-14.prompt: What happens to the depletion layer in forward and in reverse bias?

physics/ch-14.title: Depletion layer and bias
meaning: "Forward mein patla, reverse mein mota": forward bias thins the barrier and depletion layer; reverse bias widens them.

chemistry/ch-01.title: Which concentration terms ignore temperature?
chemistry/ch-01.trick: **Momos** taste the same hot or cold
meaning: **Mo**lality and **mo**le fraction (and mass %) use only masses or moles, so they do not change with temperature.
Mola**r**ity uses the **volume** of solution, which expands on heating, so it changes.
chemistry/ch-01.prompt: Which concentration terms do not depend on temperature?

chemistry/ch-01.title: What does a big Henry's constant mean?
meaning: $p=K_Hx$, so for the same pressure a larger $K_H$ gives a smaller mole fraction: the gas is less soluble.
chemistry/ch-01.prompt: Does a higher $K_H$ mean a gas is more or less soluble?

chemistry/ch-01.title: Which azeotrope goes with which deviation?
meaning: **Positive** deviation → **minimum**-boiling azeotrope (ethanol + water).
**Negative** deviation → **maximum**-boiling azeotrope (nitric acid + water).
chemistry/ch-01.prompt: Which azeotrope does positive deviation form?

chemistry/ch-02.title: Which electrode does what
meaning: Oxidation at the **AN**ode, **RED**uction at the **CAT**hode, in galvanic and electrolytic cells alike.
chemistry/ch-02.prompt: Where does oxidation happen, and where does reduction happen?

chemistry/ch-02.title: Losing or gaining electrons?
meaning: **L**ose **E**lectrons = **O**xidation; **G**ain **E**lectrons = **R**eduction.
chemistry/ch-02.prompt: Is losing electrons oxidation or reduction?

chemistry/ch-03.title: Order or molecularity?
meaning: Order is found by experiment (and can be zero or fractional); molecularity counts the species in one elementary step (1, 2 or 3).
chemistry/ch-03.prompt: Which one is found by experiment: order or molecularity?

chemistry/ch-03.title: Does the half-life depend on the starting concentration?
meaning: **Zero** order: $t_{1/2}=[R]_0/2k$ grows (zooms) with $[R]_0$.
**First** order: $t_{1/2}=0.693/k$ is fixed, whatever $[R]_0$ is.
chemistry/ch-03.prompt: Which order has a half-life independent of initial concentration?

chemistry/ch-03.title: What does a catalyst change?
chemistry/ch-03.trick: A catalyst changes **the road, not the destination**
meaning: It gives a new path with lower $E_a$, so the rate rises.
$\Delta H$, $\Delta G$ and the equilibrium constant stay the same.
chemistry/ch-03.prompt: Does a catalyst change ΔG or the equilibrium constant?

chemistry/ch-04.title: The first transition series in order
meaning: Sc, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn (atomic numbers 21 to 30).
chemistry/ch-04.prompt: List the 3d series from Sc to Zn.

chemistry/ch-04.title: Electrons taken in acid
chemistry/ch-04.trick: **Permanganate takes a handful (5), dichromate takes an over (6)**
meaning: $\ce{MnO4-}$ gains **5** electrons in acid ($\ce{Mn^7+ -> Mn^2+}$): five fingers of a hand.
$\ce{Cr2O7^2-}$ gains **6** electrons ($\ce{2Cr^6+ -> 2Cr^3+}$): six balls in a cricket over.
chemistry/ch-04.prompt: How many electrons do permanganate and dichromate each gain in acid?

chemistry/ch-04.title: Cause of lanthanoid contraction
meaning: Each added 4f electron shields the next one poorly from the growing nuclear charge, so radii shrink steadily from La to Lu.

chemistry/ch-05.title: Order of a complex name
meaning: Ligands in alphabetical order, then the metal (-ate if anionic), then its oxidation state in Roman numerals.
chemistry/ch-05.prompt: In what order are the parts of a complex name written?

chemistry/ch-05.title: cis or trans?
chemistry/ch-05.trick: **cis = sisters sit together; trans = strangers sit across**
meaning: In the cis isomer the two like ligands are neighbours (90°); in trans they are opposite (180°).
chemistry/ch-05.prompt: In a cis isomer, are the like ligands neighbours or opposite?

chemistry/ch-05.title: Spectrochemical series, weak to strong
meaning: $\ce{I-}$ < $\ce{Br-}$ < $\ce{SCN-}$ < $\ce{Cl-}$ < $\ce{S^2-}$ < $\ce{F-}$ < $\ce{OH-}$ < oxalate < $\ce{H2O}$ < $\ce{NCS-}$ < edta < $\ce{NH3}$ < en < $\ce{CN-}$ < CO
chemistry/ch-05.prompt: Recite the spectrochemical series from the weakest ligand.

biology/ch-01.title: Anther wall layers, outside to inside
meaning: **E**pidermis → **E**ndothecium → **M**iddle layers → **T**apetum (innermost; feeds the pollen).
biology/ch-01.prompt: Name the four wall layers of a microsporangium from outside to inside.

biology/ch-01.title: How many cells, how many nuclei?
meaning: The embryo sac has **7 cells** (rooms) but **8 nuclei** (people): the big central room shares two polar nuclei.
biology/ch-01.prompt: How many cells and how many nuclei does a mature embryo sac have?

biology/ch-01.title: Plants with both chasmogamous and cleistogamous flowers
meaning: ***V**iola* (common pansy), ***O**xalis*, ***C**ommelina*: their closed flowers make seed set certain.
biology/ch-01.prompt: Name three plants that bear cleistogamous flowers.

biology/ch-01.title: Order of steps in artificial hybridisation
meaning: **E**masculate → **B**ag → **D**ust pollen → **R**ebag.
biology/ch-01.prompt: List the steps of artificial hybridisation in order.

biology/ch-01.title: Coleoptile or coleorhiza?
meaning: The coleoptile sheathes the shoot apex; the coleorhiza sheathes the radicle and root cap.
biology/ch-01.prompt: Which sheath covers the radicle in a grass embryo?

biology/ch-01.title: False fruits
meaning: **A**pple, **S**trawberry and **C**ashew are false fruits: the thalamus joins the ovary in forming the fruit.

biology/ch-02.title: The path a sperm takes
meaning: **S**eminiferous tubules (via rete testis, vasa efferentia) → **E**pididymis → **V**as deferens → **E**jaculatory duct → (**N**othing) → **U**rethra → **P**enis.
biology/ch-02.prompt: Trace the path of sperms from the seminiferous tubules to the outside.

biology/ch-02.title: Parts of the oviduct, ovary to uterus
meaning: **I**nfundibulum (with fimbriae) → **A**mpulla (fertilisation) → **I**sthmus (joins the uterus).
biology/ch-02.prompt: Name the three parts of the fallopian tube from the ovary end.

biology/ch-02.title: Which hormone acts on which cell?
meaning: LH → Leydig cells → androgens. FSH (with androgens) → Sertoli cells → spermiogenesis.
biology/ch-02.prompt: On which cells do LH and FSH act in the testis?

biology/ch-02.title: Order of the phases
meaning: **M**enstrual → **F**ollicular → **O**vulatory → **L**uteal.
biology/ch-02.prompt: Name the four phases of the menstrual cycle in order.

biology/ch-02.title: Hormones made only during pregnancy
meaning: **h**CG, **h**PL, **R**elaxin. hCG and hPL come from the placenta; relaxin from the ovary.
biology/ch-02.prompt: Which three hormones are made only during pregnancy?

biology/ch-03.title: Three kinds of IUD
meaning: Non-medicated: **L**ippes loop. Copper-releasing: **C**uT, Cu7, Multiload 375. Hormone-releasing: **P**rogestasert, **L**NG-20.
biology/ch-03.prompt: Name one non-medicated, one copper-releasing and one hormone-releasing IUD.

biology/ch-03.title: Numbers in contraception
meaning: Pills: **21** days on, **7** off. Emergency contraception within **72** hours. Lactational amenorrhea works up to **6** months.
biology/ch-03.prompt: Within how many hours must emergency contraception be used?

biology/ch-03.title: STIs that are not completely curable
meaning: **H**epatitis-B, genital **H**erpes, **H**IV. The others are curable if treated early.
biology/ch-03.prompt: Which three STIs are not completely curable?

biology/ch-03.title: ZIFT or IUT?
biology/ch-03.trick: **8 and below goes to the tube; above 8 goes to the uterus**
meaning: ZIFT: ≤ 8 blastomeres → fallopian tube. IUT: > 8 blastomeres → uterus. GIFT: a **G**amete (donor ovum) → tube.
biology/ch-03.prompt: Where is an embryo with more than 8 blastomeres transferred, and what is the method called?

biology/ch-04.title: Which sex is heterogametic in birds?
meaning: Birds: female **ZW**, male ZZ, so the **egg** decides the sex. Humans: male XY, so the sperm decides.
biology/ch-04.prompt: In birds, which parent decides the sex of the chick?

biology/ch-04.title: Down, Klinefelter, Turner
biology/ch-04.trick: **Down to 21** · **Kline-fella has an eXtra X** · **Turner turns up with One X**
meaning: Down's: trisomy 21. Klinefelter's: XXY, a sterile male. Turner's: XO, a sterile female.
biology/ch-04.prompt: What is the karyotype in Klinefelter's and in Turner's syndrome?

biology/ch-04.title: X-linked recessive disorders
meaning: Both are X-linked recessive: commoner in males; the son gets the allele from his carrier mother.

biology/ch-05.title: Purines or pyrimidines?
meaning: Purines (two rings): **A**denine, **G**uanine. Pyrimidines (one ring): **C**ytosine, **U**racil, **T**hymine.

biology/ch-05.title: Which polymerase makes what?
meaning: Pol **I** → **r**RNA (28S, 18S, 5.8S). Pol **II** → **h**nRNA. Pol **III** → **t**RNA, 5S rRNA, snRNA.

biology/ch-05.title: The three stop codons
meaning: **UAA**, **UAG**, **UGA** code for no amino acid. **AUG** = methionine + start.

biology/ch-05.title: What z, y and a make
meaning: **z** → β-**g**alactosidase · **y** → **p**ermease · **a** → **t**ransacetylase.
biology/ch-05.prompt: Which enzyme does the y gene of the lac operon code for?

biology/ch-05.title: Order of DNA fingerprinting steps
meaning: **I**solate → **D**igest → **E**lectrophoresis → **S**outhern blot → **H**ybridise (VNTR probe) → **A**utoradiograph.
biology/ch-05.prompt: List the steps of DNA fingerprinting in order.

biology/ch-06.title: Homologous or analogous?
meaning: Homologous: same basic structure and origin, different function (divergent). Analogous: same function, different structure (convergent).
biology/ch-06.prompt: Wings of a butterfly and a bird: homologous or analogous?

biology/ch-06.title: Five factors that upset Hardy–Weinberg
meaning: **G**ene flow, **G**enetic drift (founder effect), **M**utation, **R**ecombination, **N**atural selection.
biology/ch-06.prompt: Name the five factors that disturb Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium.

biology/ch-06.title: Brain capacity in order
meaning: *Homo **h**abilis* 650–800 cc → *Homo **e**rectus* 900 cc → **N**eanderthal 1400 cc.
biology/ch-06.prompt: Arrange habilis, Neanderthal and erectus by brain capacity.

biology/ch-07.title: Fungi that cause ringworm
meaning: ***M**icrosporum*, ***T**richophyton*, ***E**pidermophyton*: heat and moisture help them, so groin and between the toes.
biology/ch-07.prompt: Name the three genera of fungi that cause ringworm.

biology/ch-07.title: Typhoid's pathogen and test
meaning: Typhoid → ***S**almonella typhi*, confirmed by the **W**idal test; Mary Mallon was a famous carrier.

biology/ch-07.title: Where does each kind of reproduction happen?
meaning: Asexual multiplication in the **human** (liver, RBCs); sexual fusion (fertilisation) in the **mosquito's gut**.
biology/ch-07.prompt: In which host does Plasmodium reproduce sexually?

biology/ch-07.title: Allergy in one line
meaning: Allergy involves **IgE**; **mast cells** release **histamine** and serotonin. Anti-histamines, adrenalin and steroids help.
biology/ch-07.prompt: Which antibody and which cells are involved in allergy?

biology/ch-07.title: AIDS in numbers and names
meaning: First reported **1981**; HIV copies itself with **reverse transcriptase**; diagnosed by **ELISA**.
biology/ch-07.prompt: Which test is used to diagnose HIV infection?

biology/ch-07.title: Drug and plant pairs
meaning: Heroin from ***P**apaver*; cannabinoids hit the **c**ardiovascular system; cocaine from *Erythroxylum **coca*** interferes with **d**opamine.
biology/ch-07.prompt: Which plant gives cocaine, and which neurotransmitter does it affect?

biology/ch-08.title: Who makes the holes in Swiss cheese?
meaning: ***P**ropionibacterium **sh**armanii* releases lots of CO₂, which leaves the big holes. Roquefort is ripened by fungi.
biology/ch-08.prompt: Which bacterium makes the large holes in Swiss cheese?

biology/ch-08.title: Acids and drugs from microbes
meaning: Citric acid–***A**spergillus*; acetic–***A**cetobacter*; butyric–***C**lostridium*; statins–***M**onascus*; cyclosporin A–***T**richoderma*.

biology/ch-08.title: Where methanogens live
meaning: ***M**ethanobacterium* (methanogens) work anaerobically on cellulose in cattle **rumen** and in the anaerobic **sludge** of STPs; dung is rich in them.
biology/ch-08.prompt: Name a methanogen and two places it is found.

biology/ch-08.title: Nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria
meaning: ***A**nabaena*, ***N**ostoc*, ***O**scillatoria*: biofertilisers in paddy (rice) fields.

biology/ch-09.title: Four features of a cloning vector
meaning: **O**ri (copy number), **S**electable marker, **C**loning sites (single), **S**mall size.
biology/ch-09.prompt: List the features a good cloning vector needs.

biology/ch-09.title: The three steps of a PCR cycle
meaning: **D**enaturation (heat) → **A**nnealing (primers bind) → **E**xtension (Taq polymerase, from *Thermus aquaticus*).
biology/ch-09.prompt: Name the three steps of a PCR cycle in order.

biology/ch-09.title: Which enzyme opens which cell?
meaning: **B**acteria–**L**ysozyme; **P**lants–**C**ellulase; **F**ungi–**C**hitinase.
biology/ch-09.prompt: Which enzyme is used to break fungal cells?

biology/ch-10.title: Five gains from GM plants
meaning: **S**tress tolerance (abiotic), less **P**esticide, fewer **P**ost-harvest losses, better **M**ineral use, more **N**utrition (Golden rice, vitamin A).
biology/ch-10.prompt: List the advantages of GM crops.

biology/ch-10.title: Which cry gene for which pest?
meaning: Cotton bollworm: **cryIAc** and **cryIIAb** (two genes). Corn borer: **cryIAb** (one gene).
biology/ch-10.prompt: Which cry gene protects corn against the corn borer?

biology/ch-10.title: Five uses of transgenic animals
meaning: **N**ormal physiology, **D**isease models, **B**iological products, **V**accine safety, **T**oxicity testing.
biology/ch-10.prompt: List five reasons for making transgenic animals.

biology/ch-10.title: Transgenic animal uses
meaning: Over 95% are mice. Rosie (1997): milk with human α-lactalbumin, 2.4 g/L. α-1-antitrypsin for emphysema.

biology/ch-11.title: Pyramid shapes
meaning: **T**riangle = expanding; **B**ell = stable; **U**rn = declining.
biology/ch-11.prompt: Which age-pyramid shape shows a declining population?

biology/ch-11.title: What changes population size
biology/ch-11.trick: **BIDE**: **B**irths and **I**mmigrants come in, **D**eaths and **E**migrants go out
biology/ch-11.prompt: Write the equation for population change.

biology/ch-11.title: Commensalism or amensalism?
biology/ch-11.trick: **Com**mensalism = "**Come** sit with me" · **A**mensalism = "**A**h, me hurt, you fine"
meaning: Commensalism **+/0**: the guest gains, the host is unaffected (orchid on mango). Amensalism **−/0**: one is harmed, the other unaffected.
biology/ch-11.prompt: What are the signs for commensalism and amensalism?

biology/ch-11.title: BIDE
meaning: Births and Immigrants come in; Deaths and Emigrants go out.

biology/ch-12.title: Four functions of an ecosystem
meaning: **P**roductivity, **D**ecomposition, **E**nergy flow, **N**utrient cycling.
biology/ch-12.prompt: Name the four functional aspects of an ecosystem.

biology/ch-12.title: Order of decomposition steps
meaning: **F**ragmentation → **L**eaching → **C**atabolism → **H**umification → **M**ineralisation.
biology/ch-12.prompt: Put the five steps of decomposition in order.

biology/ch-12.title: The 10 per cent law in numbers
biology/ch-12.trick: **10,000 → 1,000 → 100 → 10**: drop a zero at every step
meaning: About 10% of energy passes up each trophic level; the rest is lost, mostly as heat. So food chains rarely pass four or five levels.
biology/ch-12.prompt: If producers fix 10,000 J, how much reaches a secondary consumer?

biology/ch-12.title: The pyramid that never flips
biology/ch-12.trick: **E**nergy is **E**ver upright · **B**iomass flips in the **B**lue sea · **N**umbers flip on a **N**eem tree
meaning: Energy is lost as heat at every step, so its pyramid can never be inverted. Biomass inverts in the sea; numbers invert for a single tree.
biology/ch-12.prompt: Which ecological pyramid can never be inverted, and why?

biology/ch-13.title: India's share of the world
meaning: India has **2.4%** of the world's land but **8.1%** of its species: one of **12** mega-diversity countries.
biology/ch-13.prompt: What share of global species diversity does India hold?

biology/ch-13.title: Why the tropics are so rich
meaning: Long undisturbed **t**ime for speciation (no glaciations); **s**teady, less seasonal climate (niche specialisation); more **s**olar energy (higher productivity).
biology/ch-13.prompt: Give three reasons why the tropics have more species.

biology/ch-13.title: The four causes of biodiversity loss
meaning: **H**abitat loss and fragmentation (most important), **O**ver-exploitation, **A**lien species invasions, **C**o-extinctions.
biology/ch-13.prompt: Name the four causes in the Evil Quartet.

biology/ch-13.title: Recent extinctions
meaning: **D**odo (Mauritius), **Q**uagga (Africa), **T**hylacine (Australia), **S**teller's sea cow (Russia), plus three **tiger** subspecies (Bali, Javan, Caspian).
biology/ch-13.prompt: Name four recently extinct animals and where they lived.

biology/ch-13.title: India's three hotspots
meaning: **W**estern Ghats and Sri Lanka, **I**ndo-Burma, **H**imalaya. All 34 hotspots cover under 2% of Earth's land.
biology/ch-13.prompt: Name the three biodiversity hotspots that cover India.

english-core/reading-unseen.title: Circle the negative
meaning: The four words that reverse an item; circle them before reading the options.
english-core/reading-unseen.prompt: Which words in a question should you circle before answering?

english-core/reading-unseen.title: Lift, don't rewrite
meaning: For 1-mark short answers copy the key phrase from the text; rewrite only for inference and 2-mark items where you must show understanding.
english-core/reading-unseen.prompt: When should you lift a phrase from the passage, and when rewrite?

english-core/reading-unseen.title: NEON — circle the negative
meaning: 'Which is NOT a reason…' — circle it before reading the options; the commonest avoidable loss in Section A.

english-core/reading-unseen.title: One mark = one lift
meaning: Rewriting invites errors. Rewrite only for inference and 2-mark items, where understanding must show.

english-core/reading-unseen.title: Inference = point + evidence
meaning: State what must be true, then the phrase or fact from the text that shows it. Never infer beyond what the passage supports.

english-core/reading-unseen.title: 18–20 minutes
meaning: Section A takes 30–35 minutes of the three hours: Q1 about 18–20, Q2 about 12–15. Do it first, not last.

english-core/reading-case.title: Per cent changes
meaning: 48% to 60% = 'from 48% to 60%' or 'by 12 percentage points' — never 'by 12' or 'by 60%'.
english-core/reading-case.prompt: How do you state a change between two percentages?

english-core/reading-case.title: Link, not cause
english-core/reading-case.trick: **A survey shows a link, not a cause**
meaning: Heavier screen users sleep less = correlation within the sample; it does not prove screens cause poor sleep, and it does not prove a ban would fix it.
english-core/reading-case.prompt: What can a survey's data support, and what can it not?

english-core/reading-case.title: Percentage points
meaning: Say 'from 48% to 60%' or 'by 12 percentage points'. 'By 12' or 'by 60%' loses the mark.

english-core/reading-case.title: Quote the figure
meaning: Name the category or year and give the value with its unit — hours, per cent, people — exactly as the chart has it.

english-core/reading-case.title: Link, not cause
meaning: Infer only what the numbers support: 'students who use screens late sleep less in this sample' — not 'screens cause poor sleep' or 'students are lazy'.

english-core/reading-case.title: Rows or columns?
meaning: Reading a column for a row is the classic Q2 slip; follow a line-graph point down to the x-axis with your pencil.

english-core/writing-notice.title: Order of the frame
meaning: **I**ssuing body → **N**OTICE → **D**ate → **T**itle → **B**ody → **S**ignature (name, designation).
english-core/writing-notice.prompt: What is the top-to-bottom order of a notice?

english-core/writing-notice.title: The notice checklist
meaning: Every notice body must answer all five; each missing one costs content marks.
Contact = *the undersigned* plus a deadline.
english-core/writing-notice.prompt: Which five things must the body of a notice answer?

english-core/writing-notice.title: No I, no you
meaning: Third person or passive only. *I request you all to come* loses the expression mark; *Students are requested to…* keeps it.

english-core/writing-invitation.title: What a card never has
meaning: A formal invitation card has **no salutation** (*Dear Sir*) and **no signature** (*Yours sincerely*); it ends with RSVP.
english-core/writing-invitation.prompt: Which two letter features must a formal invitation card NOT have?

english-core/writing-invitation.title: A reply is T-O-D
meaning: Thank the host → name the occasion and date → accept or regret (with reason) → wish.
english-core/writing-invitation.prompt: What three things must every reply to an invitation contain?

english-core/writing-invitation.title: No Dear, No Yours
meaning: A formal card has no salutation and no signature. Ending with *Yours sincerely* and a name is a format error.

english-core/writing-letter.title: Shell order
english-core/writing-letter.trick: **SAD RSS**: Sender, dAte, Dear-receiver, Subject, Salutation, Signature
meaning: Sender's address → date → receiver's address → subject → salutation → (body) → close and signature.
english-core/writing-letter.prompt: In what order do the parts of a formal letter appear above the body?

english-core/writing-letter.title: Three paragraphs
meaning: P1 why you write · P2 two or three concrete points · P3 what you want done, politely.
english-core/writing-letter.prompt: What do the three body paragraphs of a formal letter do?

english-core/writing-letter.title: P-D-A paragraphs
meaning: Purpose, Details, Action. P2 is where the content marks live: places, dates, numbers, effects.

english-core/writing-letter.title: Sir, not Dear Editor
meaning: The receiver line already says *The Editor*; the salutation is simply *Sir,*. Over-formal or chatty salutations lose the format mark.

english-core/writing-article-report.title: Article paragraphs
meaning: P1 hook + issue · P2 causes and effects with examples · P3 solutions and a closing line.
Add **T-B** on top: Title, By-line.
english-core/writing-article-report.prompt: What is the paragraph plan of a 5-mark article?

english-core/writing-article-report.title: Report voice
meaning: *was inaugurated, were displayed, was given away*; no *I*, no opinion.
english-core/writing-article-report.prompt: In which tense and voice is a report written?

english-core/writing-article-report.title: Article = H-C-E-S
meaning: Hook and issue · causes and effects with examples · suggestions and a closing line. No title or by-line = format mark gone.

english-core/writing-article-report.title: Report is P-P-P
meaning: Past tense, passive voice, impersonal. *The chief guest inaugurates* or *we had fun* breaks the report's voice.

english-core/flamingo-01.title: What Franz noticed that day
meaning: Silence like a Sunday morning · the green coat, frilled shirt and silk cap · the former mayor, the postmaster and Hauser on the back benches.
english-core/flamingo-01.prompt: What three unusual things did Franz notice on entering the classroom?

english-core/flamingo-01.title: Whom M. Hamel blamed
meaning: Parents sent children to farms and mills · children put off learning · Hamel gave fishing holidays and used boys to water his flowers.
english-core/flamingo-01.prompt: Whom did M. Hamel blame for the neglect of learning in Alsace?

english-core/flamingo-01.title: Language is the key to the prison
english-core/flamingo-01.trick: Language is the key to the prison
meaning: M. Hamel's message: French is the clearest, most logical language; guard it. A conqueror attacks language to erase identity; keeping it keeps the way out. Examples: copies with France, Alsace; pigeons in German.

english-core/flamingo-01.title: Tomorrow never came
meaning: Franz, the parents and M. Hamel himself all put learning off. The loss of the language makes everyone see the worth of what they neglected — the story's second theme after language.

english-core/flamingo-02.title: Gold or wonder?
english-core/flamingo-02.trick: **Gold for the old, wonder for the young**
meaning: For parents garbage is daily bread and a roof; for children it is a treasure hunt — a rupee, sometimes a ten-rupee note.
english-core/flamingo-02.prompt: What does garbage mean to the adults and to the children of Seemapuri?

english-core/flamingo-02.title: The links of the vicious circle
english-core/flamingo-02.trick: **SMP-KBP**: Sahukars, Middlemen, Police — Keepers of law, Bureaucrats, Politicians
meaning: Six links that trap the bangle makers; fear of the police stops any cooperative; there is no leader.
english-core/flamingo-02.prompt: Name the links of the vicious circle in Firozabad.

english-core/flamingo-02.title: The vicious circle
meaning: Moneylenders keep them in debt, middlemen buy cheap, police beat and jail, the law is not enforced, politicians have no will. Add caste stigma and belief in destiny.

english-core/flamingo-02.title: Few airplanes fly over Firozabad
meaning: He will walk to a garage and learn to be a motor mechanic — small enough to be real. Asked about flying planes, he is embarrassed. The flash of daring in a town that follows fathers.

english-core/flamingo-03.title: Three attempts, not one
meaning: 1st rise: planned jump, yellowish water, nothing to grab · 2nd: legs paralysed, no scream · 3rd: effort ceases, drowsy peace, blackout.
english-core/flamingo-03.prompt: What happened on each of Douglas's three attempts to rise?

english-core/flamingo-03.title: The instructor's four steps
meaning: Belt-rope-pulley across the pool (3 months) → face under water, exhale/inhale → leg kicks at the side → all the pieces together.
english-core/flamingo-03.prompt: What were the four stages of the instructor's method?

english-core/flamingo-03.title: Only the fear of death
meaning: In the face of death he felt terror and then peace, so death did not frighten him — only its fear did. Conquering it set him free to live intensely.

english-core/flamingo-04.title: The baits of the world
english-core/flamingo-04.trick: **R-J-S-F-H-C**: Riches, Joys, Shelter, Food, Heat, Clothing
meaning: The six baits the peddler lists; the moment someone touches one, the trap closes.
english-core/flamingo-04.prompt: What baits does the world's rattrap offer, in the peddler's theory?

english-core/flamingo-04.title: Two kinds of trust
meaning: The crofter trusted without seeing — and was robbed. Edla saw his fear and trusted anyway — and was repaid. Kindness that sees the person transforms.
english-core/flamingo-04.prompt: Why did the crofter's kindness fail where Edla's succeeded?

english-core/flamingo-04.title: The world is a rattrap
meaning: The peddler's idle theory pleases him because the world has been unkind: picturing others trapped is revenge. He tests it on himself when he takes the thirty kronor.

english-core/flamingo-05.title: Shukla's trail
meaning: The illiterate peasant followed Gandhi from the 1916 Congress session city by city until Gandhi came to Champaran.
english-core/flamingo-05.prompt: Through which cities did Rajkumar Shukla follow Gandhi?

english-core/flamingo-05.title: Why 25 per cent was enough
english-core/flamingo-05.trick: **P-P-P**: Principle over sum, Prestige surrendered, Planters left
meaning: The amount mattered less than the landlords being obliged to refund; their prestige fell, the peasants learnt courage; within years the planters abandoned their estates.
english-core/flamingo-05.prompt: Give three reasons Gandhi accepted a 25 per cent refund.

english-core/flamingo-05.title: No Englishman as a prop
meaning: Relying on a sympathetic Englishman would show weakness; the cause was just and Indians must win it themselves. Champaran taught self-reliance as well as fearlessness.

english-core/flamingo-06.title: National integration in the make-up room
english-core/flamingo-06.trick: **B-M-K-A-C-A-T**: Bengali, Maharashtrian, Kannadiga, Andhra, Christian, Anglo-Burmese, Tamils
meaning: Headed first by a Bengali, then a Maharashtrian; assisted by a Dharwar Kannadiga, an Andhra, a Madras Indian Christian, an Anglo-Burmese and local Tamils.
english-core/flamingo-06.prompt: Why was Gemini's make-up department an example of national integration?

english-core/flamingo-06.title: Three facts about the English visitor
meaning: Stephen Spender: the poet who visited Gemini; editor of The Encounter; one of six ex-communists in The God That Failed — which is why the anti-communist Boss invited him.
english-core/flamingo-06.prompt: Who was the English poet who visited Gemini Studios, and how did the author finally identify him?

english-core/flamingo-06.title: National integration before the term
meaning: The department's staff came from every region, with a strict hierarchy from the chief (stars) down to the office boy (crowd players).

english-core/flamingo-07.title: Who said what against the interview
english-core/flamingo-07.trick: **N-C-K-W-B**: Naipaul wounds, Carroll horror, Kipling assault, Wells ordeal, Bellow windpipe
meaning: Naipaul: people are wounded · Carroll: a just horror, never consented · Kipling: immoral, a crime, an assault · Wells: an ordeal · Bellow: thumbprints on his windpipe.
english-core/flamingo-07.prompt: Match five writers with their complaints about the interview.

english-core/flamingo-07.title: Eco in three I's
meaning: Works in the interstices (empty time) · one set of philosophical interests across all forms · identity: academic first, novelist at the weekend.
english-core/flamingo-07.prompt: How does Eco explain his enormous output?

english-core/flamingo-07.title: Truth and art — or intrusion?
meaning: Some call it a source of truth and an art; its victims call it an intrusion that diminishes them, like a photograph stealing the soul.

english-core/flamingo-07.title: Working in the interstices
meaning: Interstices = the empty spaces of time. Remove the empty space from the universe and it shrinks to a fist; most of a day is empty too, and he fills it.

english-core/flamingo-08.title: Sophie vs Jansie
meaning: Sophie: dreamer, boutique/actress/designer, invents Casey · Jansie: realist, biscuit factory, warns her, calls it nonsense.
english-core/flamingo-08.prompt: How do Sophie and Jansie differ?

english-core/flamingo-08.title: What Sophie said about Casey
meaning: Met in the arcade outside Royce's · green eyes, not very tall · wanted an autograph but had no paper · he agreed to meet her next week.
english-core/flamingo-08.prompt: What details did Sophie give Geoff about meeting Danny Casey?

english-core/flamingo-08.title: Going places?
meaning: Ironic title: the only places Sophie goes are in her head — arcade, canal, stadium, then the biscuit factory. Barton's irony is gentle; her longing is every teenager's.

english-core/poem-01.title: The two comparisons
english-core/poem-01.trick: **Corpse in the Car, Moon at the airport**
meaning: In the car: face ashen like a corpse. At the airport: pale as a late winter's moon. Both say age and approaching death; the second is softer.
english-core/poem-01.prompt: To what two things is the mother compared, and where?

english-core/poem-01.title: Why she smiles three times
meaning: Hide her own fear · comfort her mother at parting · hope in the promise to meet again. Repetition shows effort, not joy.
english-core/poem-01.prompt: Give three reasons for the poet's repeated smile.

english-core/poem-01.title: The old familiar ache
meaning: Every child fears losing its mother; the airport parting revives it because the separation it dreaded is visibly coming. 'Familiar' is the key word.

english-core/poem-02.title: Why twelve
meaning: The clock face and the calendar — a complete cycle, small enough for anyone to spare; it frames the poem at start and end.
english-core/poem-02.prompt: What is the significance of the number twelve?

english-core/poem-02.title: The wars stanza
meaning: Green wars = against nature; gas and fire = chemical and conventional weapons; victory with no survivors = total war, a hollow win.
english-core/poem-02.prompt: What kinds of war does Neruda name, and what does 'victory with no survivors' mean?

english-core/poem-02.title: The Earth's lesson
meaning: Neruda wants no truck with death; life is what it is about. The apparent death of winter hides life getting ready — so can a human pause.

english-core/poem-03.title: What we live despite
english-core/poem-03.trick: **D-D-G-U**: Despondence, Dearth of noble natures, Gloomy days, Unhealthy ways
meaning: Keats's four causes of human suffering — the reason we need the flowery band of beauty each morning.
english-core/poem-03.prompt: What causes of human suffering does Keats list?

english-core/poem-03.title: The catalogue of beauty
english-core/poem-03.trick: **S-M-T-D-R-M**: Sun, Moon, Trees, Daffodils, Rills, Musk-rose
meaning: Then two human beauties: the grandeur of the dooms of the mighty dead, and all lovely tales we have heard or read.
english-core/poem-03.prompt: List the things of beauty Keats names.

english-core/poem-03.title: A joy for ever
meaning: Each return gives more; the joy stays and grows in memory. Beauty does not wear out like other pleasures.

english-core/poem-04.title: Why the cars stop
english-core/poem-04.trick: **C-A-T-G**: Complain, Ask the way, Turn, Gas
meaning: Complain about signs with N and S wrong and a shed spoiling the view · ask the way · use the yard to turn · ask for a gallon of gas. Never to buy.
english-core/poem-04.prompt: For what four reasons do cars stop at the roadside stand?

english-core/poem-04.title: The two oxymorons
meaning: Kind-sounding words joined to predatory ones: helpers who exploit. They relocate the poor near the theatre and store and soothe them out of their wits.
english-core/poem-04.prompt: Name the two oxymorons Frost uses for false philanthropists.

english-core/poem-04.title: Greedy good-doers
meaning: Oxymorons for false philanthropy: relocate the poor near the theatre and store, teach them to sleep all day, soothe them out of their wits.

english-core/poem-04.title: Would I accept such mercy?
meaning: He thinks of ending their pain at one stroke, then asks how he would feel if someone offered him that. Irony and honesty: pity is easy from a passing car.

english-core/poem-05.title: What the ring means
meaning: A wedding band weighs nothing; its massive weight is the burden of marriage and male domination — Uncle's ring marks her as his.
english-core/poem-05.prompt: Why is the wedding band 'massive' in weight?

english-core/poem-05.title: Aunt vs tigers
meaning: Aunt: fluttering fingers, terrified, mastered by ordeals · Tigers: prancing, sleek, chivalric, unafraid. Every quality is opposed.
english-core/poem-05.prompt: How do the tigers differ from Aunt Jennifer?

english-core/poem-05.title: Ringed with ordeals
meaning: Her terrified hands will lie still, still ringed with the ordeals she was mastered by. Her art outlives her, proud and unafraid: triumph and defeat together.

english-core/poem-05.title: Art as the free self
meaning: A feminist protest without slogans: a woman crushed by marriage pours her courage into tigers. The poem honours the art and indicts the cage.

english-core/vistas-01.title: How Charley knew it was 1894
english-core/vistas-01.trick: **G-S-D-W**: Gaslights, Spittoons, Derby hats, The World
meaning: Open-flame gaslights, brass spittoons, a wooden booth with a green-eyeshade clerk, derby hats and handlebar moustaches, an old locomotive — and The World dated June 11, 1894.
english-core/vistas-01.prompt: What details told Charley he had stepped into 1894?

english-core/vistas-01.title: Two dates
english-core/vistas-01.trick: **June on the paper, July on the postmark**
meaning: June 11, 1894 — the newspaper on the third level. July 18, 1894 — the postmark of Sam's first-day cover from Galesburg.
english-core/vistas-01.prompt: Which two 1894 dates appear in the story, and where?

english-core/vistas-01.title: Waking-dream wish fulfilment
meaning: Even stamp collecting is a temporary refuge from reality. Whether real or dreamt, the third level stands for the wish to escape into a simpler, safer past.

english-core/vistas-02.title: The numbers
meaning: Spoke at ten days; king at twenty; seventy tigers in his own state; ninety-nine before the fake hundredth; fifty rings costing three lakhs; a three-hundred-rupee toy.
english-core/vistas-02.prompt: Recall the numbers of The Tiger King.

english-core/vistas-02.title: The ending's irony
english-core/vistas-02.trick: **Missed the real, killed by the wooden**
meaning: He never killed the hundredth — the hunters did; the real hundredth tiger was a toy whose sliver infected his hand.
english-core/vistas-02.prompt: Why is the Maharaja's death doubly ironic?

english-core/vistas-02.title: Operation successful — Maharaja dead
meaning: The target: arrogant rulers who think power defeats fate, flatterers who lie from fear, officials who can be bought, and the senseless killing of a hundred tigers.

english-core/vistas-03.title: Numbers of the journey
meaning: 100 hours, 9 time zones, 6 checkpoints, 3 bodies of water, 3 ecospheres — from Madras, 13.09° N.
english-core/vistas-03.prompt: Give the numbers of Doshi's journey to Antarctica.

english-core/vistas-03.title: Phytoplankton in one line
english-core/vistas-03.trick: **Grass of the sea — small things first**
meaning: Single-celled plants that feed the whole marine food chain and absorb carbon; ozone loss lets in UV that harms them. Take care of the small things.
english-core/vistas-03.prompt: Why do phytoplankton matter, and what threatens them?

english-core/vistas-03.title: Gondwana
meaning: Warm, flourishing, no humans; after the dinosaurs died the landmass broke apart. Antarctica's ice-cores hold half a million years of carbon records.

english-core/vistas-04.title: The three options on the beach
meaning: Shelter him = treason · surrender him to the police = his death · push him back into the sea = faster death. Sadao operates first and never sends the letter.
english-core/vistas-04.prompt: What were Sadao's options when he found the prisoner?

english-core/vistas-04.title: The flashlight code
english-core/vistas-04.trick: **Two for food, one for safe, none for gone**
meaning: Two flashes: needs food · one flash: safe · no signal: he has left the island with a Korean fishing boat.
english-core/vistas-04.prompt: What did the flashlight signals from the island mean?

english-core/vistas-04.title: Why could I not kill him?
english-core/vistas-04.trick: Why could I not kill him?
meaning: At the window he recalls America's prejudice and his dislike of white faces — and still has no answer. Buck's point: the doctor's duty is deeper than the citizen's.

english-core/vistas-05.title: Mr Lamb's five lessons
meaning: Gate always open · bees sing, not buzz · no weeds, only growing things · everyone has something · hatred burns worse than acid. Plus the man killed by a falling picture.
english-core/vistas-05.prompt: List Mr Lamb's lessons to Derry.

english-core/vistas-05.title: The title
english-core/vistas-05.trick: **On the face of it = judging by appearances**
meaning: The play asks us not to; Derry's face is not Derry, a weed is a flower someone dislikes.
english-core/vistas-05.prompt: What does the title 'On the Face of It' mean?

english-core/vistas-05.title: No weeds, only growing things
meaning: Mr Lamb refuses to divide plants — or people. The same goes for bees that sing rather than buzz: attitude decides.

english-core/vistas-05.title: Hatred burns worse than acid
meaning: Acid burnt the face once; hatred of the people who stare would go on burning the self. Everyone has something — a tin leg, a burnt face, a fear of the dark.

english-core/vistas-06.title: Why the hair mattered
meaning: In Zitkala-Sa's culture shingled hair marked cowards and was cut only in mourning; long hair was dignity. Cutting it was an attack on identity, not a haircut.
english-core/vistas-06.prompt: Why did Zitkala-Sa resist the cutting of her hair?

english-core/vistas-06.title: Annan's advice
meaning: Born into their community they are given no honour; study hard, make progress, and people will come to them of their own accord. Bama stood first in class.
english-core/vistas-06.prompt: What did Annan tell Bama, and what came of it?

english-core/vistas-06.title: Hair is identity
meaning: The 'civilising' school stripped language, dress and hair. Zitkala-Sa's small rebellion is the seed of a life of activism.

english-core/vistas-06.title: Study, and they will come to you
english-core/vistas-06.trick: Study, and they will come to you
meaning: Born without honour, she can win it through progress. Bama studies with all her being, stands first, and many become her friends — resistance through achievement.
